threshold_basis.rule: Low-case trace node owner_earnings equals 13,288 USD millions (FY2025 operating cash flow of 14,193M minus capital spending of 905M per CSCO/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K filing accession 0000858877-25-000111 and CSCO/research/valuation_fact_ledger.json field normalized_owner_earnings_m).

spec.derived_from: Owner earnings, incremental returns, or reinvestment runway fall below the low-case bridge.
spec.rationale: Types the owner-earnings leg of the operating_business_and_net_assets prose falsifier. The low-case owner_earnings_reinvestment_dcf proof trace locks normalized owner earnings at 13,288 USD millions (FY2025 operating cash flow of 14,193M minus capital spending of 905M per accession 0000858877-25-000111 and CSCO/research/valuation_fact_ledger.json). If trailing-twelve-month normalized owner earnings at FY2026 year-end (2026-07-26) resolve below that anchor, distributable owner cash has fallen below the low-case bridge and the bounded per-share range should compress toward the low case (31.89 USD per share vs 58.05 base). Incremental after-tax ROIC and reinvestment-rate legs remain judgment inputs without a resolvable SEC metric and are not typed here. Historical adapter replay on Q3 FY2025 (measurement end 2025-04-26) resolved 12,803 USD millions via sec_companyfacts_ttm using normalized_owner_earnings_ttm_m_v2; resolve_spec reproduces that value when fiscal_period is set to Q3 for the replay window. Interim FY2026 TTM readings trend lower (Q1 12,733M, Q2 12,241M, Q3 11,788M per sec_companyfacts.json as of 2026-09-25), but Cisco fiscal Q4 is seasonally the strongest cash quarter, so FY-end TTM could still recover above the anchor. Target FY2026 TTM is not observable at registration (2026-09-25); FY2026 10-K is not yet in CSCO/investor-documents/DOWNLOAD_MANIFEST.json though FY2025 filed 2025-09-03, so observable_after remains 2026-09-25 pending the filing. A 34% fire probability weights the trailing decline against Q4 seasonality and historically sticky enterprise networking cash flow.
